newsitem.title: USA: Riady, Huang aided Chinese bid for Olympics - Post.
newsitem.headline: Riady, Huang aided Chinese bid for Olympics - Post.

text.p: James Riady and John Huang, two central figures in the probe of Democratic Party fund raising, worked together in March 1993 to arrange a trip to Atlanta for a high-ranking Chinese Communist Party official involved in Beijing's bid to win the Olympics in 2000, the Washington Post reported on Wednesday.

Huang and Riady arranged the visit for Zhang Baifa, the first executive vice mayor of Beijing, who traveled to speak with members of the Atlanta-based team that put on the summer Olympics in 1996, the newspaper said.

Documents obtained by the Post indicated that Huang's and Riady's company, the Indonesia-based Lippo Group, maintained a close relationship with communist Chinese and took a direct interest in supporting their ultimately unsuccessful bid for the 2000 Games.

The documents -- three internal Lippo memos -- show that Riady and Huang first sought to bring Zhang's boss, Chen Xitong, then mayor of Beijing, to the United States to push China's bid. Chen, then a member of the powerful Politburo, was a backer of the brutal 1989 crackdown on pro-democracy demonstrators at Tiananmen Square, the Post said.

Chen was placed under house arrest in 1995 in a wide-ranging corruption scandal and faced the prospect of becoming the highest-ranking official to be purged from the Communist Party in decades, according to the report.

The Lippo Group, Riady and Huang are under investigation by U.S. officials looking into foreign influence-peddling and illegal donations in connection with the Democratic Party's fund-raising activities during last year's campaign.
"The Riadys were trying to show the Chinese that they were for hire," a government investigator familiar with the memos told the Post.
"The critical question is whether the Chinese, who were willing to use them for this kind of lobbying, tasked them to do other, illegal things."
